title: Introduce policy-driven labeler and release-velocity primer for onboards
author: Aisha Patel
description: Background: onboarding noise and inconsistent release notes were creating review friction for new model imports. We want two things: (1) a stable, policy-driven labeler that harmonizes model metadata into standard operational buckets (trusted/experimental/blocked/deprecated) and stamps manifests with a small provenance hash; (2) a release-velocity primer that synthesizes a concise release-note draft from onboarding signals (ingest velocity, perf stability windows, eval sample diffs), so product and docs teams have usable notes without manual drafting. This PR introduces ingest-manifest-v2 (schema + validator), a policy labeler engine with a pluggable rule set, and a release-velocity-primer generator that produces a human-editable changelog snippet. Changes include: schema additions (velocity_score, provenance_seed, curation_hint), a policy DSL for label rules, a new CLI hook `registry ingest annotate --primer` to preview release primers, lightweight sampling hooks for eval-capture, and a short pipeline that produces a candidate changelog entry in markdown. Motivation: reduce manual curation time, improve release cadence for high-throughput model intake, and make changelogs more signal-driven. Scope & non-goals: this is not a full autogeneration of release notes; primers are drafts meant for human review. Compatibility: ingest-manifest-v2 is backward compatible for required fields; older manifests are accepted but will be enriched when reprocessed. Rollout plan: feature flag gated (registry.feature.flags.policy_labeler, .velocity_primer). We will enable opt-in for a subset of curators for two weeks before full rollout. Metrics to watch post-merge: fraction of onboards with auto-labels, time-to-first-changelog-draft, false-positive label rate (target <1%), and primer adoption (% editors using generated snippet).
commits: feat: add ingest-manifest-v2 schema and validation harness
feat: implement policy labeler engine + rule DSL
feat: release-velocity-primer generator and CLI preview hook
test: unit tests for labeler rules and primer scoring
review_comments: Priya Menon: Can you add an example rule for declining models whose hashed provenance comes from unverified buckets? (answered) — added rule 'source:is_unverified -> label:blocked' in rules examples
Ethan Liu: Primer payload looks useful but include a short confidence score and top-3 signals. (addressed) — primer now outputs 'confidence: low/med/high' and ranked signals

Camille Dubois: Are we sure ingest-manifest-v2 is backward compatible for the registry importer? We had an incident where older manifests with empty metadata fields caused crash. (addressed) — importer now has a defensive shim and a migration step that backfills defaults
QA (Darren): Found flaky test in rules_test that relied on system time — converted to deterministic seed; re-ran CI and green
release_notes:
- Add ingest-manifest-v2 with velocity_score and provenance_seed
- Introduce policy-driven labeler (trusted/experimental/blocked/deprecated) with DSL and built-in example rules
- Add release-velocity-primer: auto-draft changelog snippets derived from ingest signals and sampled eval diffs
- CLI: `registry ingest annotate --primer` to preview changelog drafts
- Backward-compatible importer shim and validator for older manifests
notes_on_testing_and_perf: Load testing: ran 5000 synthetic onboards through the labeler with batch processing; median labeling latency 38ms per manifest (p95 120ms) when label rules cache is warmed. Primer generation (including sampling hook) averaged 220ms per job in the validation harness. Unit and integration suites added; local smoke showed no regression to existing importer paths. We also added sampling gates to avoid heavy evals during bulk re-ingest. Observability: new metrics registry.labeler.latency, registry.primer.confidence_distribution, registry.onboard.velocity.histogram added to the prometheus export.
notes_on_security_and_compliance: Manifests signed by customer KMS/HSM will set 'provenance_verified=true' which policy rules can reference. The policy engine does not transmit model artifacts; only manifest-level metadata and small provenance seeds are used. Added gating to prevent primer text from echoing raw PII: primer generator redacts token patterns and strips long training example snippets by default.

human_readable_summary: This PR wires a policy-driven labeling pipeline and an automated release-note primer into the model registry onboarding flow. It standardizes manifest metadata (v2), produces quick changelog drafts from operational signals, and includes validator shims and tests. The change is feature-flagged and merged via squash.
